summary: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Palpung Sherabling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He became abbot of Palpung Sherabling Monastery around 1994.

Yongshan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt, he held professorships at Southeast, National Central, and Peking Universities, later serving as Peking University's vice-president.

Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) was a Tibetologist and historian. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a diploma at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as a research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe and held academic posts at Kobe Women's University, Otani University (ca. 2005–2017), and Bukkyo University, where he was appointed professor of Buddhism in 2014.

Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, where he was a research assistant (1986–1992), and served as associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his doctorate at Komazawa University, studying under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto, and spent his career there as a lecturer from 1971 and professor from 2001.
Yoshihiko Nasu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes serving as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and holding a post at Kongoju (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai works in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and held appointments as a part-time lecturer there and as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Center for Kyogaku and Dendo (attested 2003).

Yoshihito Muroji (born 1954) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held faculty positions at Koyasan University and Shiga University of Medical Science.

Yoshinobu Kimoto (born 1950) works in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities, and held posts as associate professor at Yonezawa Women's Junior College, president of Koshien Junior College, and professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

Yoshinobu Sakaide (1934–2020) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from 1953 to 1963, including under Mitsuji Fukunaga, and served on the faculty at Kansai University from around 1967 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe, later serving there as professor (1959–1976) before teaching at Aichi Gakuin University (1976–1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a scholar of Sinology and history. He studied at Kyoto University (1944–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (ca. 1957–1961), and worked as a library-track assistant at Kyoto University from around 1951 to 1984.

Yoshio Takeuchi (1886–1966) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He completed his studies at Kyoto University between 1907 and 1910 and served on the faculty at Tohoku University from approximately 1923 to 1947.

Yoshiro Imaeda (born 1947) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Rolf A. Stein and Ariane Macdonald, he served as CNRS director of research emeritus and advised the National Library of Bhutan.

Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, later serving as professor at Toyo, Rissho, and the University of Tokyo (chair in Japanese Buddhism, 1972–1982).

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi and served as head of Chinese Literature at Nagoya University (1955–1977) and professor at Kyoto University (1970–1974).

Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held affiliations at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and the Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshitsugu Sawai (born 1951) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned doctorates from Tohoku University and Harvard, where he studied under John B. Carman, and served as professor and Dean of the Faculty of Humanities at Tenri University (1986–2017).
